claims.quote: "I was in the smoking-room all evening," he said, short as a docket. "Mrs Harrow and I argued, certainly. We argued about money and the will. But I did not go near the library after nine." His fingers found the rim of the armchair as if they needed the furniture for a witness.
He had motive, which is not the same as guilt, and he had the look of a man who expected that to be sufficient.
"I was downstairs, laying out the supper," she said. "I heard nothing until Mr Dane came in shouting."
"Lena kept lists," Mary said. "Names, times, the sort of thing that keeps a house honest."
"We had words about pay the week before," he admitted when pressed. "But I was at the greenhouse most of the day — ask the men. I don't spend my nights in the library."
"She writes down when people come, sir. She notes times."
One page had been torn cleanly away.
I ran a fingertip along the paper where the missing sheet had once lain and found, near the sill, a fresh smear of oil that caught the light the way a small lie catches the interlocutor's eye.
On the sill sat the kitchen ashtray, a neat crescent of cigar ash in it.
"We can finish this, Mr Crowe," he said, too loudly. "There are enough reasons to call this tidy."
